about: Games Flato3D has been made to work with: what to install, the OGL3D.ini values that differ from the template, and the state of each. The installer will apply these as profiles. Candidates not yet worked on are in game_candidates.json. 'test' holds the steps for tools\analysis\gametest.ps1.

games.name: Technobabylon
notes: Rule feet: sprites stand at the depth of their bottom edge, rooms slope back towards the top of the screen.
Scissor batches: 0 = room, 1 = overlays/GUI, 2 = cursor (screen_batch 1 keeps the GUI at the screen).
Measured: character head..feet 8 px, floor at its feet 9 px, GUI 0 px (3840 px per eye).

test.reaches: title ~28 s after launch; Start at (1920,1460)
test.notes: AGS ignores SetCursorPos: move the mouse with relative steps (rmove). Starting a game rewrites Saved Games\Technobabylon\agssave.999: restore it from test-backups\Technobabylon.

games.name: Huntdown
games.api: Direct3D 11 (-force-glcore not built into the player)
notes: WineD3D's d3d11/dxgi must be the renamed copies (w3d11.dll, wxgi.dll): the NVIDIA OpenGL driver presents through the system D3D11 and would pick up a module called d3d11.dll.
WineD3D CSMT must stay on (Unity creates resources from other threads); no csmt registry key.
The game turns vsync off; swap_interval = 1 forces it on, otherwise a tear line runs across the woven picture.
Unity draws each parallax plane as its own draw call, often from one atlas: group = draw (every draw is a layer), order_curve = 0.5 gives the background planes more of the depth range.
The sprite atlas sits on texture unit 1 (unit 0 holds a 0x0 placeholder); only the units a program samples count, because WineD3D leaves earlier render targets bound on others.
The scene buffer is a texture view (render target view) and the final pass reads another view of the same texture; the composition order follows views.
known_issues: Measured on a cutscene only (layers -44..-96 px with the old depth_screen 1.05); gameplay depth to be confirmed by the user.

test.reaches: street cutscene of the first mission, then Ctrl+F12 dump
test.notes: Saves are backed up in test-backups\Huntdown (only Unity session counters change).

games.name: Door Kickers: Action Squad
notes: The loader (version.dll) is required: Steam's overlay maps the system d3d9 early and the exe has no GetProcAddress import.
WineD3D CSMT off (registry key): with it on, the title -> menu step deadlocked under the NVIDIA DXGI-layered present.
The level is drawn at about 416x234 into a 1024x1024 cache (left half colour, right half normals), then scaled to the screen: the cache is made stereo (layer cache), cache_scale = 416/1024.
F5 toggles the game's frame statistics; our hotkeys are kept from the game ([Keys] swallow = 1).
separation and depth_screen are the user's own settings.
Only a target drawn into in the same frame becomes a layer cache (WineD3D also attaches atlases to its own framebuffers for uploads).
known_issues: Depth inside the low-resolution cache moves in cache pixels (about 9 screen px per step): only a few depth levels. Planned: render the cache larger.

Now and then (seen in automated launches of DK and Huntdown, mostly the first one after replacing the DLLs) the game stops after frame 3 for about 100 s, the render thread waiting inside the NVIDIA driver under WineD3D. Not shader compilation (the program links in 43 ms on a cold cache). Cause unknown.

test.notes: Mouse clicks work (3840x2160 screen pixels), keyboard input is unreliable.

games.name: FRAMED Collection (FRAMED, FRAMED 2)
notes: screen_batch = 0: the game sets glScissor before many draws, so the AGS rule (later scissor batches are UI) would put the whole picture at the screen.
Each comic panel is drawn as frame + picture; repeated runs of the same draws share a depth, so the panels sit side by side on one plane.
Measured on the first puzzle of FRAMED: blinds +56 px, room +36..42 px, panels -2 px, hint arrow -28 px (separation 25).

The panel pictures are videos (YUV in texture1/uTexture/vTexture of program c05a6bab), so the figures arrive inside one picture. [Flat] silhouette rewrites that fragment shader: dark pixels (the black silhouettes) are sampled through a per-eye shifted coordinate and stand in front of the picture.
Silhouette check (first puzzle, separation 8.4% at the time): figures +4.8 px nearer than the panel picture (half-resolution dump), exactly the configured shift.
known_issues: Only the first puzzle of FRAMED measured; FRAMED 2 not yet tried.
A panel's picture sits slightly in front of its own frame (drawn after it).
Silhouettes come forward as flat cutouts; white details inside a figure (glasses, flowers) stay at the picture's depth, and a thin strip of background is repeated where a figure moved away.
Remote SBS check: the user preferred separation about 3% with depth_screen 1.2 (not saved).

test.reaches: first puzzle of FRAMED (collection menu -> FRAMED -> title), then Ctrl+F12 dump

games.name: Astral Ascent
install: loader/x64/version.dll (2026-10-15 or later: patches static imports)
remove: d3d11.dll, dxgi.dll, nvapi64.dll of a geo-11 install (they would load instead of WineD3D)
notes: The exe binds d3d11.dll before any of our code runs; the loader points that import at w3d11.dll (the system d3d11 stays for the GPU driver).
Every object is one quad with its own texture, drawn in layer order: drawing order gives the layers.
Text is drawn glyph by glyph into a scratch target that is cleared and composited several times a frame: each use is one layer, so lines are flat.
Animated sprites change texture every few frames: groups new to the last frame's layout take the place after the group drawn before them.
Measured in the first area (separation 25): sky +28..54 px, islands +30, swords/ruins +20..26, pillars and ground +8, player -6, HUD -14..-18.

Played through the hub areas (ruins, altar, garden, cliff) with movement, jumps and attacks: no hangs or errors, 60 fps, one A-B-A flicker that was a game effect in both eyes. Garden: sky +40..64 px, ground +28, trees +20, characters 0..-6, pergola -12, low clouds -14, HUD -20. Cliff: far islands +40..64, rock island +28, characters 0, big foreground cliff -18.
known_issues: Characters stand in front of the ground they walk on (the ground is drawn before them, so drawing order puts it farther): up to about 30 px in the garden.
Dialogue scenes: portrait, box and text are one flat UI layer in front of the scene.

test.reaches: first area after the opening dialogue (intro skipped, save slot 1 loaded), then Ctrl+F12 dump
test.notes: Loads and advances save slot 1: back up Saved Games\Astral Ascent\<steamid> first and restore it afterwards.

games.name: Guns, Gore and Cannoli 2
games.api: Direct3D 11 (the exe imports opengl32.dll, but Unity renders with Direct3D 11)
notes: The first install took the OpenGL route because the exe imports opengl32.dll, and stayed flat: Unity's output_log.txt says Direct3D 11. The installer now recognises Unity (the ggc2_Data folder) and takes the route from that log.
Same setup as Huntdown (Unity): renamed WineD3D set + loader, group = draw, order_curve = 0.5, swap_interval = 1.
known_issues: Not measured with dumps yet; depth checked by the user in play.
Windows Defender flags the x64 loader (version.dll) as Trojan:Win32/Cloxer (false positive): exclude it with the installer's [Defender exclusion].

test.notes: Saves: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\Crazy Monkey Studios\Guns Gore and Cannoli 2 - back up before play tests.

games.name: Machinarium
games.engine: Amanita Design's own engine (2020 release; Machinarium_old_32bit_DX9.exe is the old Flash version)
games.api: Direct3D 12 by default; OpenGL with the -ogl switch
notes: The exe imports d3d12.dll and opengl32.dll; it draws with Direct3D 12 unless started with -ogl. Steam does not pass it, so OGL3D appends it ([Inject] add_args = -ogl, GetCommandLine redirected before the game reads it).

With -ogl it draws fixed-function OpenGL (no shaders): orthographic sprites into one 3840x2160 framebuffer, copied to the window. The fixed-function path offsets the projection per draw; layers follow the drawing order (18-23 texture groups in the first scenes: far scrap heap, middle, props, foreground, the inventory bar in front).
It clears only the stencil buffer between masked pieces (glClear(GL_STENCIL_BUFFER_BIT)); those clears do not start a new picture, or the scene collapsed into 2-3 layers.
Renders at the native 4K: no upscale (PCGamingWiki's 'no 4K' is about the old Flash version).
Steam asks how to start it (Machinarium / Play with DirectX 9 / Play with DirectX 12): choose the first entry. The other two were not tried.

Scenes are drawn as Flash shapes with bitmap fills; pieces of the background picture are drawn again later (walk-behinds). User report 2026-10-18 (tower scene): such a piece stood out as a rectangle. A fixed-function draw that maps the same texture onto the screen exactly as an earlier picture now joins that picture's layer, unless it covers something drawn on the picture since (the ground edge over the robot's feet stays in front).

Rule feet since 2026-10-18 (fixed-function feet rule, OGL3D-SR flato3d): the scene picture is the floor sloping back (+60 top .. -26 bottom px at separation 25), walk-behinds keep its slope, the robot's parts (shadow, legs, body, head: two textures) stand together at its feet (-2 px on its ledge), a thought bubble drawn over the robot is no farther than it, the inventory bar and its icons stay at the screen. Under the order rule the robot stood ~50 px in front of the ground it walks on.
known_issues: Checked with dumps in the first scenes and the tower scene only; not played through yet.
Feet rule: tall pieces of the scene picture lean back with the floor slope (the towers); big foreground pieces reaching the screen bottom sit at sprite_min (-24 px) up to their top.

test.reaches: clicks through the intro screens, then the menu's Continue (game coordinates 1000,705; New game is at 1120,472 and overwrites the saved progress - do not click it once the user has played), then Ctrl+F12 dump
test.notes: Steam's launch chooser needs a click: for automated runs put a temporary steam_appid.txt (40700) next to the exe, start the exe itself, and delete the file afterwards. Saves: Steam Cloud, <Steam>\userdata\<account>\40700\remote\Machinarium.dat (7 slots and the settings; the Amanita-Design.Machinarium folders in %APPDATA% / %LOCALAPPDATA% stay empty) - back it up before play tests. Set output = sbs for automated checks.

games.name: Rocketbirds: Hardboiled Chicken
games.engine: PSSG (NVIDIA Cg runtime, shaders compiled with the arbvp1/arbfp1 assembly profiles)
games.api: OpenGL (ARB assembly vertex/fragment programs, no GLSL)
notes: Installed on the OpenGL route the game stayed flat: 'shaders injected 0' - the PSSG engine calls cgCreateProgram with arbvp1/arbfp1, so its draws run ARB assembly programs. The wrapper now rewrites ARB vertex programs (offset from program.env[255]) and reads the texture units of ARB fragment programs.
Forcing Cg to GLSL ([Inject] cg_glsl = 1) turned the screen white: the engine passes its own profile and assembly-only options (-profileopts MaxLocalParams=256). Keep cg_glsl = 0.
screen_batch = 0: the game sets a viewport/scissor before every pass, so later batches are not UI.
Measured (separation 17.9 set in game): chapter 1 title 'Sito in the Jungle' foreground tree silhouette near, jungle and poster wall behind; first gameplay (unloading area) -28..+44 px, median +24.
known_issues: Depth per draw only (an ARB vertex program has no geometry shader for a per-sprite spread inside one draw).
Starts with a 'connect an Xbox 360 controller' prompt (Enter continues).

test.reaches: controller prompt -> chapter 1 title -> first gameplay (unloading area), then Ctrl+F12 dump
test.notes: Saves are in the game folder's Save\ (P0-LEVEL, PROFILES, SETTINGS): back up to test-backups\Rocketbirds\Save and restore after tests. Set output = sbs before automated checks (the user watches remotely).
